html:
Kamehameha I was the Hawaiian chief who united the Hawaiian Islands into one kingdom, completing the task in 1810, and ruled it until his death in 1819. He founded the Kingdom of Hawaii.

He was born on the island of Hawaii, the big island, and was a young warrior there when James Cook arrived in 1778 and 1779. After a long war on his home island he set out to conquer the rest, using Western guns, cannon and ships, and foreign advisers. In 1795 he won the Battle of Nuʻuanu on Oahu, where many of the defenders were driven over a cliff. The ruler of Kauai, Kaumualiʻi, accepted him as overlord by agreement in 1810.

He ruled firmly, controlled the sandalwood trade with foreigners, and issued a law protecting travellers and the weak from violence. He kept the old religion and its sacred laws. Months after his death, his widow Kaʻahumanu and his son broke those laws; see Hawaii ends the kapu. The kingdom he built stayed independent until American settlers overthrew it in 1893.
